books.section: Topic 1.3 European exploration in the Americas
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

options.text: Spain was a kingdom at peace with no military ambitions left
options.misconception: Ignores the record; Spain took Granada by war and sailed the same year, not at peace.

options.text: Spain had already conquered the Americas and needed no voyage to reach them
options.misconception: Puts conquest before contact; no Spaniard had reached the Americas before Columbus sailed.

options.text: Spain's religious wars had ended, so Spain had no reason to sail
options.misconception: Mixes up the ending of one war with the end of war; the crusading habit carried into the Americas.

options.text: Spain was a crown fresh from holy war, ready to carry its mission overseas

rationales.general:
1. Ask what January means. Granada fell, ending centuries of holy war in Iberia.
2. Ask what October means. Columbus landed in the Caribbean, nine months later.
3. Ask what connects them. The same crown, the same soldiers, and the same language of holy war.
4. Rule out the others. Spain was not at peace, the wars did not end ambition, and no conquest came before contact.
Remember: when two events share a year, ask what the first gave to the second.
rationales.D: Granada fell in January and Columbus landed in October of the same year. Spain carried its soldiers, its ships, and its crusading mission straight from Iberia to the Americas.
rationales.A: Spain took Granada by war in January 1492 and Columbus landed in the Caribbean in October of the same year. A kingdom at peace does not do both.
rationales.B: No Spaniard had reached the Americas before Columbus sailed in 1492. Conquest could not come before contact.
rationales.C: The Reconquista ended, but the crusading habit did not. Spain carried its soldiers and its mission straight into the Americas.

stem: In January 1492 the Catholic Monarchs took Granada, ending the Reconquista. In October 1492 Columbus landed in the Caribbean. What does the pairing of these two events in the same year best show about Spain in 1492?

stimulus.source_note: Original summary sentence; the Reconquista ended with the fall of Granada in January 1492.
stimulus.text: Spanish conquistadors described their campaigns in the language of holy war, seeking gold, glory, and royal favor in the name of the Catholic faith.
